STI-288DGGPM
8-port Gigabit L2+ managed industrial PoE switch with 2× 1G/2.5G SFP uplinks, integrated DI/DO/RS485 I/O channels, and 240W total PoE budget.

Native DI/DO/RS485 interface via removable 8-pin terminal block, eliminating the need for an external serial gateway
1-channel digital input (12V–30V) and 1-channel digital output (normally open/closed/pulse, 2A@30VDC) enable direct alarm triggering, relay control, and event-driven automation
RS485 serial server supports Modbus RTU transparent transmission over TCP/IP, seamlessly connecting legacy PLCs, RTUs, meters, and field sensors to modern IP networks
Dedicated RS485 LED indicator provides real-time TX/RX status visibility for instant serial link diagnostics
2. Dual 1G/2.5G SFP Uplinks for Cost-Effective Fiber Aggregation
Two multi-rate SFP slots support 1GBase-X and 2.5GBase-X, providing flexible fiber uplink options for medium-distance or EMI-sensitive environments where copper is unsuitable
Dual-rate flexibility allows the same hardware to adapt to both existing 1G fiber infrastructure and emerging 2.5G backbone upgrades without device replacement
SFP DDM (Digital Diagnostic Monitoring) enables real-time optical transceiver health monitoring for proactive maintenance in unmanned field deployments
G.8032 ERPS ring protection across SFP uplinks delivers ≤20ms automatic failover, ensuring continuous operation in redundant fiber ring topologies
3. 8-Port PoE+ with Intelligent Power Management and Full L2+ Feature Set
All 8 RJ45 ports support IEEE 802.3af/at PoE+, delivering up to 30W per port with a 240W total power budget for cameras, APs, VoIP phones, and industrial sensors
Per-port PoE priority, power scheduling, PD watchdog, and alarm threshold configuration ensure reliable power delivery and remote PD fault recovery without on-site intervention
Comprehensive L2+ management: VLAN/QinQ, IGMP v1/v2/v3, ACL, 8-queue QoS (SP/WRR), 802.1X, DHCP server/relay, SNMP v2c/v3, MQTT, sFlow, plus IPv4/IPv6 static routing
Hardened industrial design with IP40 fanless housing, Din-rail mounting, -40°C to +75°C operating range, 6KV surge protection, and redundant 44–57VDC power input
Application: IP surveillance networks, industrial automation edge nodes, smart transportation cabinets, oil & gas remote sites, utility substations, and any deployment requiring serial legacy device integration with fiber uplink redundancy in a compact DIN-rail form factor.

STH-2C24XF-HSI
Half-width L3 managed switch with 24×10G SFP+ fiber and 2×100G uplinks — two units combine into one 1U slot.
3 Core Highlights
1. Half-Width Form Factor — Two Units, One 1U Rack Slot
Compact 21.5×4.4cm half-width chassis fits two switches side-by-side in a single standard 1U rack space
Each unit operates as a fully independent switch — or pair them via MLAG for Active-Active dual-node physical redundancy
Delivers the reliability of two separate switches at the rack footprint of one — purpose-built for space-constrained AV and enterprise deployments
Built-in SDVoE API Server on each unit eliminates the need for a separate SDVoE controller
2. Dual Hot-Swap Power Modules + Hot-Swap Fan Modules
Two independent 550W CRPS hot-swappable power supplies switch seamlessly on mains loss — in-service power replacement with zero traffic interruption
Hot-swappable fan modules (front-to-back airflow) allow cooling maintenance under full-load traffic without pulling the unit from the rack
MTBF ≥90,000 hours with hardware watchdog and process monitoring for continuous operation in mission-critical environments
3. 24×10G SFP+ All-Fiber Access + 2×100G QSFP28 Uplinks
24 optical SFP+ ports deliver low-latency 10G connectivity to servers, AV endpoints, and access layer devices — no copper interference
2×100G QSFP28 uplinks provide non-blocking backhaul to aggregation or spine layer at 880 Gbps switching capacity
Hot-swappable SFP+/QSFP28 transceivers support mixed single-mode and multi-mode fiber on demand — no module changes needed when topology evolves
Application: SDVoE Pro AV broadcast networks, enterprise/campus aggregation, space-constrained data center edge, high-density fiber access deployments.
